title: Bowing versus picking the bass
summary: Dawson claims to have started the four-four picked rhythm; bows suit waltzes and vocal numbers.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Did you do much picking in the old days, Eddie?

Yeah, practically, I started off with a bow. You know what I mean? The bass? Yeah. I started off with a bow, too. But, I did more picking after, you know. I started right down. I believe I'm the first one that started that four-four rhythm. I had a way used to pick with one finger, you see. Yeah. That four-four rhythm and that's where it popped for. George Foster, he caught it for me and from that on, all the rest of them started it. Oh, what was it before, Eddie? There you go.
Okay, it's going again. You were talking about the bass and picking.
Yeah, all of the bands practically used to use bows, bass-filing bows. They used to play with more bass with their bows than picking, you see.
Well, when they played with that bow, what would they be playing? They wouldn't be playing four-four?
Yeah, they'd play dance, regular dance. It's like they're playing now with the coaster. They're just using the bow instead of thumping it with their fingers, you see.
But it was still the same...
Yeah, same time, yes. The same time.
Well, what does the picking do? It makes it more...

It makes it, I don't know, more jazz, you know. Yeah, most staccato. Yeah, like that. Better than the bow, you see. Now, they still use bows on these big bands now. They have to... Some of these numbers, they got to use the bow on them, you know. Because the sentimental pieces, you know, it requires the bow. Yeah. And the baseball players now with all these big bands, it's playing that kind of type of music now. They use the bow and then put it down, take them, turn it around on their finger then, when they get to a part where they have to pick, you know.
Did you say, you say, sentimental tunes, like waltzes and things like that?

Well, they have some waltzes, they have to... it goes better with the vocals, better with them waltzes too, you see. But it's something like... the songs like you're singing, you see, like vocal songs, like those fellas women singing or like that, you know.

Yes, it requires... it sounds better with a bow, you know, than picking with your fingers. Because it's a slow... it's a different type of time. Different time that you've got to give. You can't use that four-four rhythm with that, you see. You got... you got different time that comes in and calls for that vocal stuff, you see.
